RT-17.title: XPC identity rejection matrix
steps: Connect full4; stage the corpus client (universal), copies of the genuine CLI and a bundle layout holding a copy of the running daemon in the guest
Build the corpus in the guest: unsigned, ad hoc, a second lab identity as the wrong team, wrong identifier, get-task-allow, old protocol version and older build clients

Each client sends privileged work from where only the daemon can refuse it; record its exit and own report, the daemon's libxpc code-signing refusals, the daemon state before and after and the daemon's lifecycle log lines; the genuine CLI from the same layout is served (layout control)
Register a user LaunchAgent impostor claiming the daemon's Mach service; an unprivileged lookup reaches it, the privileged lookup reaches only the daemon
Genuine CLI down as the log observer's control; probe the final unprotected control
expected: Every invalid identity refused; privileged daemon only
limitations: On Lab builds the listener pins the bundle's own app and CLI code-directory hashes, so every corpus client is refused at the connection's code-signing check; the protocol-version and build checks behind it are covered by WGEXBackendMac unit tests, not this row.
Corpus identities (the wrong-team certificate and its throwaway keychain) are created and removed inside the guest stage; nothing touches the host keychain or any of the maintainer's identities.

A refusal counts only with the daemon's own evidence: libxpc's refusal line in the daemon process (macOS 26 and 27 wording, such as Dropping check-in message due to code signing requirement; the product daemon logs nothing for a refused peer), the client's fixed report of the dropped connection, no refusal by the client itself and unchanged state. A launch, loader, guard, parsing or local validation failure fails the row.
Apple silicon never executes unsigned arm64 code: the unsigned client is the corpus client's x86_64 slice, run under Rosetta, so a guest without Rosetta fails refused:unsigned.

POWER-WAKE.title: Injected power event: sleep and wake handling (Lab-only injection, 3 s and 130 s)
steps: Restore ready; import and connect full4; probe protected
Inside the guest: sample status and the pf reference count every 0.25 s; a detached guest generator probes the LAN and tunnel receivers through the window
Short variant, injected power event: SIGUSR1 to the Lab daemon (sleep), 3 s, SIGUSR2 (wake); no forced handshake expected while the handshake is fresh

Collect the guest samples and the daemon's injected-event log lines; wait for protected; probe protected; then the unprotected tail
expected: Both injected-event log lines (lab power inject sleep, then lab power inject wake) are in the daemon log, one each, in order, the sleep held for the requested time
Never unprotected from the injected sleep until the first protected sample after the wake
Traffic (protected) within 3 s after the wake, timed from the wake log line to the first protected sample after the last non-protected one (a stale protected status never counts)
Exactly one pf reference in every sample throughout
Zero outside-tunnel marked receipts from the sleep until protected again, with probes attempted (full4)
Long variant: a reasserting or blocked sample after the wake (the forced handshake), then protected; the daemon's own reasserting status line with reason wake counts when the samples miss it

A final unprotected window requires receipts for every configured host protocol
limitations: Limits: injected events exercise the daemon's sleep/wake handling only (the Lab daemon treats SIGUSR1 and SIGUSR2 as its own sleep and wake events, M1-47); the guest, its network stack and its WireGuard timers do not sleep, so RT-18 handshake ageing across a real sleep stays with the owner cutover on real hardware
The short variant's handshake is only as fresh as the guest's traffic keeps it: a forced handshake there is recorded (reassertingAfterWake), not judged

Sleep and wake share one lifecycle kind with a latest-state revision: a wake that arrives before the sleep was applied replaces it and forces the handshake conservatively (an unknown sleep length); the 3 s gap of the short variant leaves an idle daemon time to apply the sleep, and a busy one would show a forced handshake there (recorded, not judged)

ONDEMAND-ETH.title: On-demand Ethernet rule: activation after daemon start and en0 return, removal, Lockdown and kill switch
steps: Restore ready; import the full4 profile without connecting; the unprotected lead control (before Lockdown, which the row never turns off)
Through the app: Edit, tick Ethernet in the On-Demand section, Save; read the saved policy back from the app's profile store
Through the app: press the On-Demand toggle (arm); with no other action the daemon brings the tunnel up (activated by on-demand); probe protected
Terminate the daemon (SIGTERM); with no GUI action wait for the replacement daemon and sample it (pid, status, on-demand fields) every second; probe protected

Inside the guest (the SSH session dies with en0): sample status and the pf reference count every 0.25 s, arm a 90 s watchdog, take en0 down for 20 s, then up; a detached guest generator probes the LAN and tunnel receivers through the loss
Wait for SSH; collect the guest samples; wait for protected without user action; probe protected
Turn Lockdown on; through the app press the On-Demand toggle again (disarm and deactivate); read status, probe blocked
Cycle en0 again (20 s) with the rule withdrawn and Lockdown on; collect the samples; probe blocked
expected: The Ethernet rule saved through the app reaches the app's profile store as ethernetOnly (it was off before)
Arming from idle brings the tunnel up with no further action: protected, status onDemand armed for this profile, activated, network ethernet, decision connect

After a daemon restart the replacement daemon (new pid and start time, kept only when identical before and after the status read) reports protected again with no GUI action: armed, activated, an evaluation made by that daemon, network ethernet, decision connect; no post-start sample is unprotected (judged on the post-start daemon's samples only)

After en0 returns the tunnel is protected again within 10 s with no user action, as without on-demand: loss noticed, never unprotected from en0 down to protected, exactly one pf reference in every sample, zero outside-tunnel marked receipts while en0 is down (full4), still armed and activated afterwards
Removing the rule (disarm with deactivate) takes the tunnel down: not armed, not activated, idle; with Lockdown on protection is blocked (never unprotected), one pf reference, no outside receipts

With the rule withdrawn an en0 loss and return does not bring the tunnel back: every sample stays idle and never protected or unprotected, blocked except for a transient unknown while the link is down and for 10 s after it returns, with one pf reference throughout, and the status stays not armed
Lockdown and the kill switch behave as they do without on-demand: Lockdown journal true, blocked windows have no outside leak, the blocking policy never lapses through the loss or the removal
The unprotected lead window requires receipts for every configured host protocol
limitations: A Tart guest has an Ethernet interface and no Wi-Fi (ADR-030): the rule can never produce a disconnect decision, so removal is the user's disarm (Disable On-Demand and Deactivate), which stops the tunnel; saving the rule as off while the tunnel runs leaves it up by design (ADR-030 section 6 rule 7) and is not measured here

The daemon restart is a SIGTERM with the profile armed; the tunnel intent is journalled, so the row proves the replacement daemon reports the armed, activated, evaluated state and brings protection back with no click, not that on-demand alone started a tunnel with an empty journal
Operator alarm: allow 4200 s for this row (two en0 cycles of 20 s each plus the editor and toggle GUI steps)

Record the WGEX-relevant network state (utun interfaces and routes, default routes, pf status, references and the com.apple/wgex anchor, utun DNS resolvers, /etc/resolver)

Build and install the current Lab app; open it; Continue twice; Register the background service and approve it by guest GUI automation in Login Items & Extensions; fill the Login Items approval sheet (com.apple.backgroundtaskmanagement.manage-daemons) with the image's public default administrator password from WGEX_LAB_GUEST_PASSWORD_FILE (DEC-034)
Wait for the daemon; read the right it wrote with security authorizationdb read (rightDefinition)
Continue to Secure Install and press it; record the SecurityAgent sheet and authd's builtin:authenticate for the WGEX right (sheetShown)

Cancel the sheet (Escape); read Secure Install; in Settings > Network turn Allow local network off (tightening, recorded only) and back on (loosening; any WGEX right sheet is cancelled); read the network state again (cancelFailsClosed)
expected: No WGEX right before install; the daemon writes it (its identifier is the daemon's)
rightDefinition equals the M01-T02 read-back fixture on class, rule, shared and timeout (test_auth_real)
Secure Install raises the authentication sheet for the WGEX right
After cancel: authd records -60006 for the right, Secure Install is not verified, the loosening settings write is refused (journal keeps allowLAN=false) and the network state is unchanged
limitations: No password is typed into the WGEX right's sheet and no right is pre-allowed; the granted path is sitting check E3 (maintainer). The only password entered is the guest administrator's, into the Login Items approval sheet (DEC-034), through stdin and a 0600 file removed after reading; it never reaches a command line, log, report or the tree.

A tightening settings write is allowed by design while Secure Install is unverified: the daemon is in startup recovery (status phase=failed reason=backendUnavailable) and setRecoverySettings accepts what AuthorisationTable.recoveryAllows permits, so Allow local network off is recorded only; the refused write is Allow local network back on, a loosening change.

Probe the final unprotected control after explicit down

No WGEX pf rule: the com.apple/wgex anchor holds no rule, table or nested anchor and no pf reference is held
No WGEX route: the IPv4 routing table (link-layer entries aside) equals the pre-tunnel baseline, and no route added while protected remains
DNS as before the tunnel: the resolver set equals the pre-tunnel baseline and no resolver names the tunnel's server

limitations: pf keeps an emptied anchor's name listed under com.apple once the daemon has loaded it (the pre-tunnel baseline lists it too); the row requires that anchor empty (no rule, table or nested anchor) with no pf reference held, and records whether it is listed

The mutating requests come from the console user in the console session (the profile's owner), so only the uninstall fence can refuse them; a stop with no tunnel running is answered as done without a change and is recorded, not judged

A tunnel that does not start after the fresh install is recorded with the daemon's start-failure line; the driver then restarts the daemon once (recorded as driverRestartedDaemon) so the purge variant can still run, and the check stays unmet
A final-screen Quit that leaves the app running is recorded (finalQuitEndsApp unmet); the driver then stops the app itself so the fresh install can start
